# Blackjack Card Counting Trainer

> A web trainer for Hi-Lo card counting. It teaches the running count, the
> true-count conversion, basic strategy and the Illustrious 18 / Fab 4
> deviations, then lets you apply them at a simulated multi-seat casino table
> and shows, from your own recorded sessions, where your edge is leaking.

Card counting is not a trick or a secret system. It is a small, measurable
advantage — roughly one to two percent — that only materialises over hundreds
of hands, and only if the count is held accurately, basic strategy is played
exactly, and bets are sized to what the shoe actually says. The trainer exists
to turn that from knowledge into reflex.

## What it covers

- [Hi-Lo counting](/): the balanced level-one system real counters use — 2–6 count +1, 7–9 count 0, tens and aces count −1
- [True count](/): running count divided by the decks remaining in the shoe
- [Basic strategy](/): the correct play for every hand against every dealer upcard, for both S17 and H17 rules
- [Deviations](/): the Illustrious 18 and Fab 4, each with the true-count threshold at which the count overrides basic strategy
- [Shoe simulation](/): six decks, 312 cards, configurable penetration, cut card checked only after a completed round

## Training modes

- Speed Drill — hold the running count under time pressure
- Flashcards — every basic-strategy hand, and when to deviate
- Deck Estimation — judge remaining decks from the shoe
- Bet Spread — size bets by true count
- Casino Session — a full multi-seat felt table with bots, splits, doubles and payouts
- Analytics — accuracy trend, practice heatmap, weakest hands, real edge from recorded sessions

## Access

- Free tier: Speed Drill, Flashcards, basic strategy chart, personal analytics, levels and achievements. No payment details required.
- Pro subscription: the full casino session, deviations overlaid on the strategy chart, and bankroll / risk-of-ruin tools.

## Notes

- This is a practice tool. It is not affiliated with any casino and does not
  offer gambling or real-money play.
- Counting cards mentally is legal; casinos are private businesses and set
  their own rules.
- The user-facing app at /app requires an account and contains only per-user
  data — it is not useful to crawl.
